o1.biggest_strength: Very usable structure with clear bundle jobs, sensible discount levels, good break-even thinking, and a safe test plan focused on profit per visitor.
o1.biggest_mistake: The free-shipping math undercounts the orders affected by moving from ₹499 to ₹599, and it makes lip balm a discounted main bundle instead of mainly using it as the natural cart add-on.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make face wash + vitamin C serum the lead routine bundle or explain the trio more cleanly, fix the ₹599 affected-order math, and add a sharper COD/RTO move such as prepaid-only free shipping or a COD fee under ₹499.

o2.biggest_strength: It uses the lip balm correctly as a cart add-on, takes COD/RTO seriously, gives practical test design, and avoids risking the serum reorder by jumping the threshold too quickly.
o2.biggest_mistake: The bundle break-even math is a little inconsistent, and the recommendation says keep ₹499 while also proposing a ₹699 test, which needs a cleaner decision path.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the bundle economics, make the face wash + serum routine the obvious hero offer, and turn the shipping recommendation into a clearer staged plan: keep ₹499 now, test lip balm add-on, then test COD/prepaid-specific rules before any sitewide threshold rise.

reason: I would rather hand Output 2 to the team because it spots the real leak in small COD orders and uses lip balm as the right add-on instead of over-discounting it. Output 1 is good, but its threshold math is shakier and its first bundle choice is less aligned with how customers already buy.
